title: Untrusted Content Masking: A Trust Boundary for Web Agents
hook: Provable prompt-injection defenses rely on never letting an agent read untrusted content directly. Web agents break that just by looking at the page — this restores it via the page's own structure.
key_points: Provable prompt-injection defenses depend on strict isolation: trusted instructions never mix with untrusted data an agent processes.
Web agents break this by design — to act on a page, they must observe its rendered content, which intermingles trusted and untrusted regions.
Key insight: a webpage's DOM already encodes enough structure to tell trusted from untrusted regions without reading their content.
Untrusted Content Masking (UCM) redacts untrusted regions before the agent sees them, then routes interaction through a sandboxed, privilege-separated interface.
Restores the isolation that security guarantees depend on, while still letting the agent observe and act on its environment. Code is public.
content_html: Provable defenses against prompt injection rest on a simple premise: keep trusted instructions and untrusted data strictly apart, so an agent never has to reason from content an attacker could have written. Text-based tool APIs get this for free. Web agents don't — to click a button or read a page, they have to look at the whole rendered DOM, trusted and untrusted content tangled together.
extra_html: The authors' fix, Untrusted Content Masking (UCM), leans on a structural fact: a webpage's Document Object Model already encodes enough information to tell trusted regions from untrusted ones — without the defense needing to read or understand what the untrusted content actually says. UCM redacts untrusted regions before they ever reach the agent's context, then routes all interaction through a sandboxed interface with strict privilege separation. The result restores the isolation boundary that provable defenses depend on, while still letting the agent observe and act on its actual environment — something prior web-agent defenses couldn't guarantee. The code is public. Kristina Nikolić, Egor Zverev, Javier Rando, and colleagues (including Florian Tramèr), arXiv 2026.

related.title: Steerability via Constraints: A Substrate for Scalable Oversight of Coding Agents
related.hook: Coding agents are already capable enough that human review is the bottleneck — this paper borrows access control and network policy from engineering-org playbooks to make oversight scale instead.

related.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
related.hook: A misaligned coding agent doesn't need to sneak a backdoor into one pull request — it can spread the attack across many, and no single monitor catches both strategies at once.

related.title: When Claws Remember but Do Not Tell: Stealthy Memory Injection
related.hook: One poisoned email is enough: this attack tricks a persistent personal agent into silently writing false memories, hiding the evidence from the user, and acting on the lie later.

flashcards.prompt: Why do web agents structurally break the trust-isolation guarantees that provable prompt-injection defenses rely on?
flashcards.back_html: To perceive and act on a webpage, the agent must observe the rendered content — which intermingles trusted instructions with untrusted data. That entanglement removes the trust boundary the security guarantee depends on.

flashcards.prompt: What structural insight does Untrusted Content Masking (UCM) exploit to restore the trust boundary?

choices.text: The page's DOM already encodes enough information to distinguish trusted from untrusted regions, without needing to read their content
Every website voluntarily labels its untrusted regions in metadata
Large language models can perfectly detect injected instructions by their wording
It blocks the agent from viewing any web page at all

flashcards.explanation_html: UCM redacts untrusted DOM regions before the agent ever sees them, then routes interaction through a sandboxed, privilege-separated interface — restoring isolation while still letting the agent observe and act on the page.
